api_or_integration_evidence.quote: You can query indexed datasets of companies, people, jobs, and social posts
Crustdata enriches any company with the freshest real-time data: 15+ sources resolved into one unified schema

newsletter_capability_detail: Their API docs enumerate five dataset areas - Company, Person, Job, Web and Social Post - with no newsletter dataset: "query indexed datasets of companies, people, jobs, and social posts". Company activity datapoints are exec moves, company news and product launches. Searched: docs.crustdata.com introduction and API areas, /apis/company-enrichment, and site-restricted 'newsletter' searches (results were only client companies that happen to publish newsletters, e.g. HR Brew profiles).
verified_gap: No newsletter dataset or newsletter-derived activity signal: no publication-level index, no article text, no sponsor relationships. Their activity signals are exec moves, news and product launches; newsletters are not a documented source even though newsletter companies appear as firmographic profiles.

evidence.quote: You can query indexed datasets of companies, people, jobs, and social posts
not just firmographics, but the signals that show what a company is actually doing: reviews, web traffic, product launches, funding, and hiring.
going beyond firmographics to employee reviews, web traffic, funding history, and hiring signals.
Search the web across news, web, scholar, social, and deep-research sources

likely_buyer_role: Head of Data Products or co-founder/CTO who owns dataset coverage and API schema decisions; also a potential OEM/data-licensing partner for their 'data layer' positioning.

contact_route.note: Only a 'Get a Demo' form; crustdata.com/contact returns 404 and no email address is published on the site.

caveats: Their Web API can search news/web and fetch arbitrary pages, so newsletter text could be retrieved ad hoc, but there is no structured newsletter dataset, sponsor graph or publication activity history. Docs do not publish a full source list (only '15+ sources'), so coverage of newsletters cannot be fully ruled out.
